title: Prove shared-writer and restart recovery through the review workbench
description: add-workbench-spa:2.1. RED: stale initial commit, stale response, explicit supersession, two independent clients, duplicate delivery after restart, cancellation after display, lost acknowledgement and incompatible storage fail their public/visible expectations. GREEN: wire typed shell results into the workbench and durable adapter without duplicating core decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Real browser reload restores completed/pending/changed reviews and original provenance. Two independent shell/adapter instances share one database and yield one applied response and one conflict. Lost ack after actual durable write blocks mutation until reconciliation, including reconstruction. Stale drafts stay visible but require explicit fresh review; no silent revision rebinding. Existing history survives all cases.

title: Deliver the minimal artifact-review workbench through the public shell

acceptance_criteria: Browser flow shows identity/revision/content/request, accepts feedback and shows recorded outcome for that revision. Uses durable adapter and public shell only; no duplicate revision/policy/lifecycle logic. Diagnostic fault controls are separate from reviewer controls. No authorization or external action is inferred. First path passes; final recovery acceptance stays open in wanna-9r2.

title: Implement durable local review storage with atomic conditional writes

acceptance_criteria: Use real durable browser storage in acceptance, not only a fake. Independent connections cannot both apply conflicting writes. Reopen preserves receipts and pending operation identity; reconciliation cannot infer no-effect from transient absence. Typed failures and declared scope match companion design. Adapter tests pass before workbench depends on it.

title: Restore review lifecycle and reconcile uncertain outcomes

Unknown effects block mutation across reconstruction until authoritative applied/not-applied proof. Empty receipt alone never permits retry. Resume preserves completed/pending/changed/unresolved state and provenance; corrupt or unsupported storage is preserved with recovery_required.

title: Tambor-rendered review-shell demo: composition-shell through tambor widgets (was y9d.2 wanna half)
description:
From the tambor-y9d.2 descope ruling (Rule-of-5 review of the re-routing proposal, verdict NEEDS_REVISION -> revised): the wanna review-shell session demo (tambor-on-wanna distillation, ~140 lines with mini-tambor) must NOT be rebuilt as demo-local logic on the tambor side — the shell semantics (five typed submit outcomes, conditional commit, reconcile, restart durability) are wanna's corpus semantics, already implemented and spec'd: @wanna/composition-shell barrel (openReviewSession + typed outcomes) and the review-workbench capability. Re-implementing them as tambor demo-local code is the same anti-pattern the y9d.2 anti-goal names (mini-tambor: duplicated fake-library code), mirrored.

WHY NOW: this demo is the second consumer of the same shell — review reuse evidence, the gate wanna-zbn (distribution prep) is waiting on. review-baseline is the hand-owned baseline; a tambor-rendered shell strengthens the reuse evaluation.

SCOPE: examples/review-tambor/ (family naming: review-workbench, review-baseline, review-headless) — mount the REAL openReviewSession projection through tambor's widgets (gallery slider/textarea/button vocabulary, plain-data state via the interop seam makeOpsApp). Demo-local logic limited to the view mapping (projection -> tambor Elem) and a demo-local fault-injecting ReviewPersistencePort wrapper (infrastructure, explicitly allowed — lose-ack and storage-down fault buttons need it; NOT a semantics copy).

ACCEPTANCE (concrete, per the reuse precedent): the demo satisfies the EXISTING tests/review-workbench/reuse-scenarios acceptance scenarios (current/stale/restart, the review-baseline bar) through the tambor-rendered UI; must gate: npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json exit 0 (examples/ is in tsconfig include — CI typechecks it) AND the demo runs a scripted fixture round trip asserting the five typed outcomes render. Meter: just ci green.

IMPORT MECHANISM (decided — EDGE-001 verified): tsconfig path alias '@tambor/*' -> ../tambor/src/* (the @wanna/* source-alias precedent, no package prerequisite), plus a ci.yml actions/checkout of charly-vibes/tambor at the pinned rev c8ec467156da4abd9110bbcf3b7da56bbd745639 into ../tambor so CI typecheck resolves it. Pin bump rides tambor releases. Rejected: git submodule (workflow overhead), vendored tgz (binary in git).

ANTI-GOALS: no shell semantics copies (the projection comes from the real barrel); no tambor code vendored into wanna's published surface (wanna is private:true — moot but stated); no changes to tambor's dist/spa.js or published package for this.

1. Revert pre-push jobs in lefthook.yml to unwrapped commands (keep the fix wiring).
2. Delete tools/gate-timing.sh and drop .gate-timing.log from .gitignore.
3. Optionally keep tambor-style permanent timing if the suite decides ongoing gate-cost measurement is worth a wrapper — tambor kept theirs (tambor-j44); decide before removing.

Before removal, capture the before/after comparison from .gate-timing.log into the charly-fx4 thread (baseline: wanna pure-push median 197s this week).

title: Repair existing corpus OpenSpec required-section compatibility
description:
## Problem
Full OpenSpec strict validation fails all 30 unchanged deployed specs on required sections. Both revised change proposals pass. Specodelic corpus lint passes with three existing observability advisories.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run openspec validate --all --strict from the repository root.
2. Observe 30 failed deployed specs and two passing changes.
3. Run openspec validate interaction-engine --strict; observe the missing Purpose/Requirements required-section diagnostic.

## Expected Behavior
The deployed corpus is readable by the repository's required validation tools without weakening its properties or scenario bindings.

## Actual Behavior
The OpenSpec parser rejects the deployed section structure while specodelic accepts the corpus.

## Implementation Shape
RED: reproduce against the existing corpus. GREEN: reconcile required sections with specodelic semantics, retaining deployed conformance bindings. Diagnose corpus formatting versus tool compatibility first. Keep this maintenance task separate from first-review implementation; no domain behavior changes.
acceptance_criteria: All deployed specs pass OpenSpec strict validation and spk lint; existing scenario-to-contract bindings and executed tests remain intact. Record whether this is corpus formatting or tool compatibility before changing files.
notes: Diagnosis (recorded before batch edits): corpus formatting, not tool compatibility. Each of the 30 legacy deployed specs lacked a '## Purpose' header (purpose prose sat unlabeled after the H1) and its single '### Requirement:' block's paragraph lacked SHALL/MUST; interaction-need additionally had one non-SHALL paragraph. OpenSpec strict surfaced these one layer at a time. Fix: insert '## Purpose' before intro prose; add SHALL to requirement paragraphs ('Each declared model transition SHALL be carried by...'; interaction-need need-SHALL). Scenario VERIFIES bindings, Model tables, Properties untouched. Executable verification: new openspec-gate (openspec validate --all --strict, ~1s) in lefthook pre-commit + just ci.

title: Tidy review composition after consumer acceptance without behavior changes
description: add-composition-shell:4.1. Separate refactoring ticket and commit. Refactor only duplication or boundary friction exposed by the completed slice; rerun existing contracts unchanged. If no justified tidy is needed, close with that evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Same public API, behaviors and acceptance outcomes before/after; existing consumer, adapter and recovery tests pass. No features or compatibility changes mixed into refactor. Record concrete simplification or no-op rationale.
close_reason: RED falsifiability: mutated submitCommand (skip preconditions + silent retarget to current revision); recovery contract 'stale feedback explained' caught it (1/20 failed); restored GREEN. Tidy: renderArtifact() moved artifact field display into dom.ts (handlers no longer mutate display fields); freshReviewButton() dedupes 4 duplicate .demo-fresh-review queries. Same public API, all contracts unchanged: vitest 770, tsc/eslint/pretender clean, spk lint 0, ah overlay 367 passed (+1 known no-toml owned by zcq). Commit 193504a.

title: Evaluate review reuse with a second consumer and direct implementation baseline
description: add-workbench-spa:3.1. Define a bounded comparison protocol before building the second client. RED: the headless client must fail the same current/stale/restart expectations until wired to the public API. GREEN: satisfy them using the same shell and adapter contract. Compare to a small application-specific state machine/persistence implementation satisfying identical acceptance scenarios. Do not modify the core silently to manufacture a reuse success.
acceptance_criteria: Retain report and reproducible scenario evidence. Count consumer-owned coordination code and imports; record time, author familiarity, excluded setup and adapter costs. Separate first-build and marginal second-consumer effort. Record core changes required. Favorable reuse requires no new core behavior and less consumer-owned coordination than baseline; otherwise record revise/narrow/defer. Record explicit proceed/revise/narrow/defer distribution decision; test counts alone are not value evidence.
close_reason:
add-workbench-spa:3.1 complete (commits 47b390f, 9acdb39, 7b70f53 + feature commit on top of 5452a93).

Comparison protocol defined first (docs/reuse-comparison.md): one shared current/stale/restart acceptance suite (tests/review-workbench/reuse-scenarios.ts) run unchanged against both implementations.

RED→GREEN: headless consumer (examples/review-headless, 187 lines, imports ONLY @wanna/composition-shell, port injected) + direct baseline (examples/review-baseline, 190 lines, own state machine + JSON-snapshot store). Both pass the identical 6-test suite; both implement idempotent reopen.

Report bound to disk by reuse-report.test.ts (contract counts must match sources). reuse-comparison-complete TOML bound: workbench overlay ah check --run-tests = 368 passed, 0 findings. Falsifiability executed both ways: baseline dedup mutation → gate reports test-failing:1; report section removal → contract failure.

Measured: zero core changes (src/ untouched — verified); 1 public import; favorable-claim condition 2 (less coordination) is inconclusive on LOC (187 vs 190, margin is gate-forced formatting noise; pre-split baseline was 159) and the trivial baseline store flatters the baseline. DECISION: NARROW — semantic reuse demonstrated, distribution (wanna-zbn) not unblocked by this LOC evidence; re-run with a realistic baseline store or narrow the distribution claim to semantic reuse. Report exists per the change, so archival can proceed regardless.

title: Distribution scoped to semantic reuse (narrow decision recorded; LOC evidence inconclusive)
description: Deferred follow-up after add-workbench-spa:3.1. Review recorded proceed/revise/narrow/defer outcome before starting. If proceed, draft the distribution change and select the smallest package topology supported by consumers. RED: a fresh consumer fails to import/run the emitted public entry and typecheck declarations. GREEN: implement build, exports/files and host boundary checks. A workspace split requires demonstrated need. No npm publication is authorized by this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Before implementation, reuse report exists and records proceed; otherwise remain deferred or re-scope. Distribution proposal approved. Emitted ESM and declarations work in a fresh supported consumer outside repo aliases; source compile excludes test globals; supported runtime/module combinations explicitly documented; no transitive host dependency. Publication remains separate explicit authorization.
notes: add-shell-distribution change drafted, Rule-of-5 reviewed, approved, and implemented: @wanna/composition-shell emitted (esbuild bundle + tsc declarations), fresh-consumer verification green outside repo aliases, 7 scenarios bound, overlay ah check --run-tests 400/0. Distribution prep done; npm publication remains separately unauthorized per ticket.

comments.author: charly vibes

Re-scope chosen per the decision record's path (b): distribution claim narrowed to semantic reuse. Coordination-line distribution stays gated on path (a) — re-run the comparison with a realistic baseline store (can fail, conflict, lose acknowledgements) so exclusions stop flattering it.
